title: Buildings the City rents that sold or pay no tax, and their landlords' ties
question: Do the landlords whose buildings sold during a City lease, or who pay no property tax on a building the City rents, show other ties?
finding: 10 of the 23 rented buildings that changed hands or carry an exemption also carry a landlord tie in older screens. Most: 845 Jackson Street (Chinese Hospital Association): autopilot: Exempt property where flagged organizations are registered (Chinese Hospital Association); exceptions: The same supplier, excused from competition year after year (Chinese Hospital Association); exceptions: The largest contracts awarded without competition (Chinese Hospital Association) and 3 more.
how: Rows of housing_supply "buildings the City rents that changed hands after the lease" and "buildings the City rents whose owner pays no property tax on them" were matched to the older property, parcel, officials, lobbying and contract screens by landlord name and by street number and name.
limits: A lease binds a buyer and a sale during a lease is ordinary. A welfare exemption applies where the building is used for the exempt purpose, and a nonprofit renting space to the City may still qualify. Campaign gifts are by people who list the firm as employer. Landlords who are individuals are not named. Name and address matches only.
